lesson.title: Three More Letters: ਘ, ਙ, and ਚ
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: You already know eight letters! Today we finish the row we started yesterday and begin a new one: ਘ (ghagga), ਙ (nga), and ਚ (chacha).

ਘ (ghagga) makes a heavier 'gh' sound, related to ਗ but with more breath. ਙ (nga) makes a soft nasal sound, like the 'ng' in 'sing'. ਚ (chacha) makes a 'ch' sound, like in 'chair', and starts a brand new row. Practice saying: gha... nga... cha.
You now know eleven letters! You've finished a whole row of the Gurmukhi alphabet and started another. Tomorrow we'll review everything you've learned this week.

objectives: Recognize and name the letters ਘ (ghagga), ਙ (nga), and ਚ (chacha)
Notice that ਘ and ਙ complete the sound-family row started with ਕ, ਖ, ਗ, while ਚ begins a new row
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review all eight letters learned so far — can the child name them in order?
2. Introduce ਘ, ਙ, ਚ one at a time, saying each name aloud together three times.
3. Point out that ਘ and ਙ finish the row started yesterday (ਕ ਖ ਗ ਘ ਙ), and ਚ starts a new row.
4. Trace each letter in the air before picking up a pencil.
5. Move to the worksheet: trace each letter, then write it once more on the practice line.
6. Close by reciting all eleven letters learned so far, in order.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on ਙ's nasal sound separately, since it's the most different from the others and often needs extra practice
Ready for more: ask the child to sort all eleven letters learned so far into their two completed/started rows
For a child who enjoys a challenge, have them write all eleven letters from memory before checking against the worksheet
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and recognition activity — check that each traced letter roughly matches the shape shown.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: ਘ and ਙ complete the first consonant row, and ਚ begins the second — continuing the systematic Painti Akhari sequence and building toward this week's cumulative review.
